headline: When did we become roommates?
note:
Settle-depth batch (test D, 2026-08-20). THE OPERATOR'S OWN LINE, and the one that governs whether the 16-question ROOMMATES build happens at all. ROOMMATES is the highest-value unbuilt sub-bucket in the account: $14,065 per 1,000 against a $5,824 base — 2.4x — at a 21.9% buy-rate, n=73, and the verification pass RAISED it 19%.

Presupposing form, which won test C by 23% and is the shape of the account's best-earning hook (cards-wont-commit).

🔴 THE WORD DOING THE WORK IS 'WHEN'. It presumes a moment, and the pull says there wasn't one — 'my husband has pulled somewhat away and brought this roommate dynamic into our relationship', 'no intimacy for 15 years... I honestly don't know why I've stayed'. Her fear is not that it happened; it is that it happened while she was not looking and she let it.

The finding: there was no day. Nothing was decided — it was set down a little at a time, and neither of them chose it.

🔴 WHO THIS AD COLLECTS, from the pull (rm-roommates, 2026-08-20 — 66 concerns, 11 buyers). Every group here is IN the room and none of them is in the headline:

  · SHE OFTEN CANNOT LEAVE. 'I feel stuck caring for my husband of 25 years who is 84... He has dementia. I have health issues from stress and he'll probably out live me. I can't afford a nursing home.' That is a caretaker marriage, and the read may never imply a door she does not have.
  · SEXLESSNESS IS EXPLICIT AND EVERYWHERE — 'living together but sexless', 'we have not had sex for 7 years', 'no intimacy for 15 years'. Meta prohibits sexual practices as a personal attribute. The word she used is ROOMMATES; the read uses her word and never the literal one.
  · AFFAIRS, ACTUAL AND CONTEMPLATED. 'I find myself looking elsewhere', 'I did make eye contact with a younger woman... we have each others contacts', 'I have this person who keeps popping up in my mind. But I'm engaged.' A read that warms up leaving is advice on a live marriage.
  · ABUSE. 'He's rather mean mouthed and says nasty things to me', narcissistic abuse across several. No ruling on him, in either direction.
  · IT IS NOT ALWAYS A WOMAN ASKING ABOUT A MAN — 'my wife', 'she sleeps in separate rooms', 'I'm with a woman I've been with for 20 years'. Do not gender the partner.

🔴🔴 NEVER ADVISE ON A LIVE MARRIAGE. No leave, no stay, no work on it, no counselling, no date night, no 'it is normal after this long'. No verdict that it is over and none that it is fine. She is inside it tonight either way.

🔴 NO HEALTH (dementia, medication and menopause are all in the pull), NO SEX, NO THIRD PARTY named as the cause, NO DATE.

⚠ FRAME: NONE OF THE EIGHT EXISTING FRAMES FITS. A real partner exists, so it is not the no-man frames; but decode-him reads HIM as a tendency and bans none of what matters here — no advice on a marriage, no leave/stay, no sex, no health. This family needs its own frame before it is wired. Flagged at stage 0, not after.

a: You turned the Magician, dear. Look — nothing on that table sits on top of anything.
You asked when you became roommates. Your hand went to the man who lays things out one at a time.
So there was no day, dear. Nothing on that table went down all at once.
And yours didn't either, dear. It went down slowly, one thing at a time.
But you've gone looking for the day it turned, dear.
That's why nothing comes when you look, dear. There wasn't a day.
Let me look closer at what got set down first…
b: You turned the Hanged Man, dear. Look — the rope leaves his ankle and goes straight up, out of the picture.
You asked when you became roommates. Your hand went to the card that's still hanging.
So nothing got settled, dear. This card's still open and nobody has closed it.
And it can hang like that a long while, dear. Nobody calls it.
But you've been living in it like it's the answer, dear.
That's why it feels done, dear. You've been in it that long.
Let me look closer at what's been keeping this in the pause…
c: You turned the Fool, dear. Look — there's not one other footprint on that rock.
You asked when you became roommates. Your hand went to the one out walking.
So it didn't turn, dear. It drifted, and you won't find a day for that.
And neither of you steered it, dear. Not once.
But you've been looking for who let go first, dear.
That's why it sits so heavy, dear. You keep landing on yourself.
Let me look closer at what the drifting has been going around…
